title: Choose the visual world for Sub-Sub
question: The roll assigned The Natural-History Plate. Keep it, take my pick or the category standard, or re-roll.

options.label: The Natural-History Plate
options.lineage: Engraved natural-history plates, 1820-1850: Beale's Natural History of the Sperm Whale (1839) and Scoresby's Arctic Regions (1820), the plates Melville read
options.thesis: Every claim is a figure. Sub-Sub is shown the way a plate shows a specimen: each part numbered, labelled with a leader line and captioned, so the page proves what the tool does instead of saying it.
materials: the plate mark (the pressed border of a copperplate)
letterpress captions with a true italic
options.viewport: PLATE I, framed by a plate mark. The browser view at work is the specimen, drawn large, with Fig. 1 to Fig. 5 labelled by leader lines: the preview, the evidence line, a quote with its page link, Undo, the mode. Left of it, the legend: the name, one line on what it does, and the install command with its OS tabs, the primary action. Below, the italic caption that explains the figures.
options.risk: Tips into museum-precious if the plates become ornament; every label must point at something real and the page must stay fast for a clinician with ten minutes.

raised.raise: State is drawn by line, never by colour alone: full text a solid rule, abstract dashed, metadata dotted; previewed, applied and undone each with their own mark.
Rows are live entities in a fixed grid: tool rows and library results change state in place, without reflowing the plate.
The install path is one numbered sequence with one default action at each step.
Processes are shown as stages with a still record of each result: the flow of works, the screening log.
Every figure and diagram has a full text equivalent: captions for figures, a table for the flow.
Only the figure in focus is fully inked; the rest of the plate rests in plate tone until pointed at.

options.label: Melville's Marginalia
options.lineage: The pencil marks in the books Melville owned (Melville's Marginalia Online): underlines, X marks, ticks and notes in his Shakespeare and Milton
options.thesis: Sub-Sub reads the way Melville read: the interface's marks are a reader's pencil marks, and every quote, question and check looks like a mark made in a real book.
options.viewport: An open spread: on the left page the product's claim set as text with pencil underlines; on the right, the margin where Sub-Sub's checks sit as notes, with the install command written as the last note.
options.risk: Pencil on a pale page is where most bookish designs land; it needs a ground and colour that refuse the cream-and-serif default, or it reads like every literary site.

options.label: Normalled Jackfield
options.case: Fuses poorly: neither students nor clinicians see themselves in a patch bay, and it loses the Moby-Dick brief; its state grammar is strong.
options.kept: State drawn by stroke pattern, never by colour alone.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.case: Fuses poorly: works as departing trains is a stretch for a reading tool, and it is far from the brief.
options.kept: Live rows that change state in place without breaking the grid.

options.label: Shareware Installer
options.case: Fuses poorly: retro novelty, and it reads as a joke beside research.
options.kept: One linear sequence with one default action per step.

options.label: Raku Smoke Flash
options.case: Fuses poorly: chance and smoke are the opposite of checked evidence.
options.kept: Processes as stages, with a still record of each result.

options.label: Miura-Fold Sheet
options.case: Fuses poorly: elegant engineering with no line to readers or libraries.
options.kept: Every diagram keeps a complete accessible equivalent.

options.label: Code Cascade Terminal
options.case: Fuses poorly: the hacker register is the generic AI-tool look the brief rules out.
options.kept: Only the item in focus is fully legible; the rest rests until pointed at.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A research-tool product site at full craft: white ground, a clean sans, a large product screenshot, one blue accent, features in a grid.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and install command on the left, the browser view on the right, features below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every AI research tool by design, which is the look you ruled out.
